primitives.name: Blocking Constraint Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: The tackle's work when the point of attack is on his own side, inside or outside of him, requires that he shall block or box his opposing tackle long and successfully, until the play can be carried by.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_b': 'Force of block (N)', 't_b': 'time of successful block (s)', 'L_b': 'length of block path (m)'}
primitives.assumptions: Opposing tackle exerts constant force; block duration is deterministic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When F_b < F_o (opponent force), block fails.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian model computes P(block success | F_b, F_o); GSE state transition maps L_b to play continuation.

In the offensive regime, the tackle must maintain a stable constraint against the opposing tackle, ensuring that the play can proceed through a controlled opening. This is modeled as a force equilibrium problem where the block must sustain F_b > F_o for duration t_b. The defensive regime demands continuous spatial coverage, represented by D_t = dA/dt, where A is the area under defensive responsibility. Tactical proficiency P_p ensures that both regimes operate without conscious deliberation, enabling rapid response to dynamic changes in play structure. The duality arises from the fact that the same physical and mental resources are deployed in both contexts, yet their functional roles differ. Failure modes include insufficient block duration (t_b), inadequate practice (P_p), and poor spatial coverage (D_t).
